complexity.correctness_reason: Recursion is one frame per character and the limit is hard-set to 2000, so any word longer than ~1998 characters — allowed once the 1000-character cap is lifted — raises RecursionError on insert/search/startsWith.
complexity.notes: Each operation re-slices the string at every level, which is what costs O(L^2); ||walking the characters iteratively (or recursing on an index into the original word) removes the copies and gives O(L) per operation||. sys.setrecursionlimit(2000) is re-executed on every node construction, since each child is a new PrefixTree — it only needs to run once, and arguably the design would be cleaner with a separate node type rather than making every node a full PrefixTree. The added `import sys` fixes the previous version's NameError. On CPython 3.14 nothing annotation-related matters here.
complexity.space: O(T) total for the trie, where T is the number of characters inserted across all words, plus O(L) recursion stack per call
complexity.summary: A recursive trie where each PrefixTree node holds a dict of children and a terminal flag; insert/search/startsWith peel off the first character and recurse on the remainder of the string.
complexity.time_average: O(L^2) per operation, where L is the word/prefix length
complexity.time_worst: O(L^2) per operation: each recursive level copies the remaining string via word[1:], summing to O(L^2); dict lookups are on single characters from a fixed 26-letter alphabet, so no adversarial collision degradation
